data.title: EU vows to fix 'China Shock 2.0' via talks with Beijing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Plastics safeguards probe appears closest to launch, Sefcovic says
  • Goods trade deficit with China exceeds €1 billion a day
  • EU agreed with Beijing to halve vehicle imports from China

By Philip Blenkinsop and Padraic Halpin

The European Union should focus on dialogue with Beijing to curb imports of products such as chemicals and machinery to rein in a damaging trade deficit with China, EU ministers said on Friday, as the bloc considers import quotas for plastics.

European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic earlier this month agreed with Beijing for the EU to cut imports of hybrid vehicles from China by more than half to address a deficit that has swelled to more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) a day, and to support Europe's struggling carmakers.

Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee told a news conference after a ministerial meeting in Dublin that all EU members were determined the Commission should continue dialogue with Beijing

"There's a very clear desire for us to move beyond that (hybrid cars) and to look at other areas, chemicals, machinery. There's a number of issues, agrifood sector, and areas that have been mentioned," she said.

She added that, while dialogue was the priority, the Commission could use existing trade defence tools itself to resolve some imbalances.

Sefcovic told the news conference he had heard every trade minister's views on which sectors should be the next priorities for trade measures.

PLASTICS SAFEGUARDS NEXT IN LINE

He continued that an investigation into safeguards for plastics appeared to be the next to be launched.

"Currently, I think the plastics sector is the closest," he said. "We are looking into whether all the requirements to launch an investigation are in place."

He appeared to be referring to a request for measures to curb imports of PET, the plastic widely used in packaging, which lawyers told Reuters earlier this month had been submitted.

China needs foreign buyers for the flood of relatively cheap state-subsidised goods its own shoppers can't absorb, and the EU is torn between welcoming those imports to ease living costs and keeping them out to rebuild its own factories.

The EU's goods trade deficit swelled to more than €370 billion ($414.25 billion) in 2025 and is on course to break well past €400 billion this year, a situation European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called "unsustainable".

European industry says the export surge, dubbed China Shock 2.0, is already causing factory closures and job losses, most notably the 100,000 positions set to go at Volkswagen.

China has said in the past it is not the root cause of the EU's problems, but a partner in solving them.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said this week there were growing concerns for chemicals and machinery. Lithuania Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said on Friday that pharmaceuticals could also be included.

France's junior minister for trade, Nicolas Forissier, said dialogue was only possible now that the EU was speaking as one.

Chinese authorities "understand when you are clear, when you speak frankly, when you are firm on your positions," he said.

($1 = 0.8914 euros)

data.title: Stocks mixed, day after AI-related selloff; oil prices rise again
data.description:
Key points:
  • Wall Street stocks mostly lower
  • Oil prices extend recent gains
  • US Treasury yields up; France gets respite

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Marc Jones

Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

The Nasdaq was up 0.2% after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1%.

An index of semiconductors was up about 1%. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade.

It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity."

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.

US crude rose 2.56% to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74%. European natural gas prices jumped.

AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL

Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.5% after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.

Telecom company shares, including Verizon , dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9%, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX eased 11.14 points, or 0.14%, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21%, to 26,062.75.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 1.64 points, or 0.15%, to 1,121.29.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4%.

Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4% earlier.

US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992%. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June.

EURO FALLS

The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.

French yields (FR10YT=RR), which were down 5 basis points at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.

A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.

France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday.

The euro was last down 0.12% at $1.12 , set to end the week 0.35% lower.

data.title: Midterm Elections Could Have Meaningful Impact on Yields — Market Talk
data.description: The outlook for Treasury yields "is highly dependent on Middle East conflict, Ukraine, Russia [and] potentially midterms," DWS's George Catrambone says. November's election could determine the future of the war in Iran, which has been driving oil prices, he says. "Ultimately 10-year yields have been fairly well correlated to the price of oil." Catrambone says the pace of investment on artificial intelligence infrastructure can also be affected by the midterms. Given the uncertainties, his investment strategy is "to be nimble." Catrambone likes high-grade corporate bonds that are trading at a discount, while selectively adding lower quality yields aiming at a "strongly yielding portfolio and one that is diversified." data.title: Tech stocks sound an uncomfortable 2008 echo
data.description:
By Robert Cyran

The industry is now 40% of the S&P 500. A sharp sell-off on AI fears is a reminder that such lop-sidedness marked prior booms and busts. Unlike the dotcom era, frenzied activity is lifting earnings faster than valuations. The financial crisis shows that this can be a bigger risk.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky.

CONTEXT NEWS

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index fell 2.6% on October 22, its biggest one-day fall since June. Tech giant Meta Platforms fell 7%, while chipmaker AMD declined 8% and peer Micron fell 6%.

data.title: Corn, soy basis bids mostly steady-stronger
data.description:
Spot basis bids for corn and soybeans were mostly steady to stronger in the US Midwest on Friday, reflecting demand from grain handlers as a weeks-long slide in Chicago Board of Trade corn futures curbed farmer selling and the soybean harvest neared completion in some areas, merchandisers said.

  • The spot corn basis firmed by 4 to 5 cents a bushel at ethanol plants in Illinois and Iowa, and by a penny at a Cincinnati, Ohio, elevator.

  • The corn basis improved by 1 to 5 cents at two Midwest river elevators, where grain is loaded onto barges for shipment on the Mississippi River toward Gulf Coast exporters.

  • For soybeans, bids improved by 9 to 16 cents at two river elevators, reflecting demand from Gulf exporters following a series of US soybean sales to China since mid-October.

  • However, the soybean basis weakened by 5 cents at a Toledo, Ohio, terminal.

  • Among domestic processors, soybean bids were steady to firmer, with the basis improving by 5 cents at a Morristown, Indiana, crushing facility.

  • Some Indiana farmers were nearly finished harvesting soybeans and were moving on to corn, two grain merchandisers said this week.

  • CBOT December corn (CZ26) was down 4-1/4 cents at $4.56-1/4 per bushel in midday trading, hovering near a three-month low set on Wednesday, while November soybean futures (SX26) were up 4-3/4 cents at $12.57-3/4 a bushel, rallying from a near two-month low set this week.

data.title: Godrej Properties Q2 profit declines 62% to ₹154 crore
data.description:
Godrej Properties reported 62 per cent decline in its consolidated net profit in second quarter of FY27 to ₹154 crore due to higher operating costs.

In the same quarter last year, the company reported net profit of ₹405 crore.

Total revenue rose 38 per cent y-o-y to ₹2,575 crore. However, the value of booked properties declined 6 per cent to ₹8,008 crore due to the deferral of some property launches to the third quarter. The company sold 3,658 units during the second quarter with a total area of 6.2 million square feet.

Total expenses rose 90 per cent to ₹2476 crore on a y-o-y basis. EBITDA declined 72 per cent to ₹171 crore.

‘Strong quarter’

“While some of the headline earnings and bookings numbers for the quarter look muted, Q2 was a very strong operating quarter with sustenance sales growth of 83 per cent y-o-y to ₹5,054 crore and cash collections growth of 31 per cent y-o-y to ₹5,318 crore. We only launched one third of our expected annual launch pipeline in the first half of the financial year and were still able to deliver 43 per cent of our annual bookings guidance highlighting the continued strength of underlying demand in the sector,” said Pirojsha Godrej, Chairperson, Godrej Properties Ltd.

“We remain confident of surpassing our full year guidance across all key operating metrics. We are especially focused on generating strong cash flows and expect ₹15,000 crore of collections and ₹7,000 crore of operating cash flow in H2 FY27. This will allow us to both invest for continued growth while being free cash flow positive for the period,” he said.

data.title: Kobelco targets 3% growth in excavator market, launches three new models
data.description:
Kobelco Construction Equipment India (KCEI) expects India’s hydraulic excavator market to grow around 3 per cent this year, despite a slowdown in National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) project execution, supported by infrastructure spending by State governments on urban development, irrigation and rural roads.

The market for hydraulic excavators, excluding mini excavators, is expected to increase from around 31,000 units last year to 32,000-33,000 units this year, Moses Eddy, Director, KCEI, told businessline.

new variants

Meanwhile, Kobelco on Friday launched three excavator variants in the 19.1-24-tonne category manufactured at its Sri City facility in Andhra Pradesh. The new range targets mining operators, major road contractors, smaller contractors and equipment rental companies, says a statement.

The company is looking to penetrate markets in parts of Jharkhand and Maharashtra, where smaller contractors and rental players seek economical equipment.

Localisation and exports

Kobelco’s Sri City plant has an annual production capacity of 3,500 units and has manufactured more than 20,000 machines for domestic and export markets across over 16 countries. The company has invested around ₹900 crore in the facility since 2011.

Production is currently around 2,800-2,900 units annually, and KCEI expects to reach full capacity in about two years, depending on market acceptance and export demand. Exports account for roughly one-third of its volumes, with the Middle East, Africa and neighbouring countries among its target markets, he said.

Localisation in the new models has increased from 48 per cent to 68 per cent, primarily through the use of a locally sourced Cummins engine instead of the Hino engine used earlier.

KCEI reported turnover of more than ₹2,000 crore last year and expects it to rise to ₹2,400-2,500 crore this year, he said.

Jun Hayama, Managing Director, KCEI, said the launch coincides with the company completing two decades of its presence in India, including manufacturing and engineering operations.

Eddy expects changes in government tender norms and quality standards to improve infrastructure project execution in the coming months. However, geopolitical uncertainties and shipping constraints could affect exports.

On Chinese competition, he said manufacturers from China had expanded overseas sales partly because of excess capacity following the slowdown in the country’s real estate market. T

heir market share in India, which had risen to around 40 per cent, has since declined to about 33-34 per cent, Eddy said.

data.title: IndusInd Bank PAT at ₹1,176 crore as provisions dip and other incomes increase
data.description:
IndusInd Bank posted a standalone net profit of ₹1176 crore as the private bank halved its provisions in the quarter-ended September 30 2026, as against a loss of ₹445 crore in the year ago period. The bank however increased its net profit by 17.3 per cent sequentially.

The bank’s net interest income (NII) increased 3.6 per cent to ₹4569.5 crore in the reporting quarter as against ₹4409.4 crore in the corresponding quarter of last year. Sequentially, the NII dipped 2.46 per cent from ₹4684.7 crore in the previous quarter.

The bank faired better in terms of other income which includes treasury incomes. The line item improved 36.3 per cent to ₹2,246.8 crore as against ₹1,648 crore in the year-ago period.

The bank’s advances grew 14.95 per cent to ₹3.63 lakh crore in the recently concluded quarter as against ₹3.16 lakh crore in the year-ago period. Deposits grew 7.2 per cent to ₹4.3 lakh crore in the second quarter of the current fiscal from ₹4 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter of previous fiscal. “Under the RBI swap window, we mobilised $3.5 billion dollars of FCNRB deposits. This implies a market share of 2.5 per cent, well above our natural market share of about 1.5 per cent on overall deposits,” Rajiv Anand, MD and CEO of the bank told analysts. Bank lent about ₹16,564 crore in Q2FY27 to FCNR(B) related deposits.

The FCNR(B) inflows reduced net interest margin (NIM) by 9 basis points to 3.23 per cent in Q2FY27 form about 3.32 per cent in Q2FY26. The measure dipped 54 basis points from 3.57 per cent in the previous quarter.

A large part of the turn to profitability came on top of a 53.2 per cent dip in provisions to ₹1216 crore in the reporting quarter from ₹2622.38 crore in the year ago period. “This was due to lower net slippages in the quarter,” said Viral Damania, Chief Financial Officer of IndusInd in the analyst call.

The bank’s non-profitable assets as a share of gross advances reduced to 2.73 per cent, as against 3.6 per cent in the year-ago period. NNPA as a share of net advances was stable at 0.83 in Q2FY27 but improved 12 basis points from 0.95 per cent previous quarter.

data.title: India’s smartphone market records poorest Q3 in a decade this year
data.description:
New Delhi, October 23: India’s smartphone market declined by 20 per cent year-over-year (YoY) in the third (Q3) quarter this year, the poorest performance in the last one decade, a report by Counterpoint research said on Friday.

Entering 2027, the market is likely to remain on a challenging footing, as higher device prices continue to extend replacement cycles and limit volume recovery, it said in the Monthly India Smartphone Tracker report said adding that record-high memory prices drove up device costs, pulling down shipments for most brands.

It also said that amid persistently soft demand, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) held back on channel inventory, even ahead of the festive season.

Device Prices

“Rising component costs pushed device prices higher, putting increasing pressure on affordability and weakening the traditional mass-market volume engine, particularly below ₹15,000...Sub-₹20,000 shipments declined by 47 per cent in Q3 2026 as rising model prices pushed devices into higher price bands,” Shubham Singh, Research Analyst at Counterpoint Research said.

Consumers became more selective, extended their replacement cycles and deferred upgrades, while OEMs prioritised margin protection, portfolio rationalisation and leaner channel inventory over aggressive volume expansion ahead of Diwali, he said.

“Looking ahead, we expect India’s smartphone market to shrink by around 13 per cent in 2026, with continued pricing pressure weighing on affordability and replacement demand. The post-festive seasonal slowdown will add to the pressure, while elevated component costs are likely to drive another round of price hikes after the festive season sale,” Tarun Pathak, Research Director, Counterpoint Research said.

The impact is already visible in the mass market, where OEMs are restructuring portfolios by introducing more 4G and lower-specification models and trading down specifications across some price segments to manage costs while maintaining price points, he said.

Affordability

Going forward, growth opportunities will increasingly shift toward the premium and upper-mid segments, while the mass market remains under pressure from affordability constraints and tighter OEM margins, he mentioned.

“With upfront prices rising, no-cost EMIs, exchange offers and retailer-led promotions will become increasingly important conversion levers, helping consumers manage higher upgrade costs,” Pathak added.

In terms of market share, with a 17 per cent share in Q3 2026, Samsung reclaimed the top spot in the market after nine quarters, the report said adding that Samsung’s relatively measured price hikes and proactive management of rising memory costs helped it outperform the overall market.

Apple Sales

Vivo (excluding iQOO) was in second place in Q3 2026, with a 16 per cent share, followed by Oppo, retaining its third position with a 12 per cent market share, and Xiaomi (including POCO) ranked fourth with a 12 per cent share.

Apple has seen a strong start to the iPhone 18 Pro series in India, with initial sales nearly 20 per cent higher YoY than those of the iPhone 17 Pro series. Continued demand for the iPhone 17 line-up points to healthy consumer interest, even as Apple adjusts pricing across its portfolio amid rising memory and component costs, it added.

data.title: CSB Bank PAT up 14% on NII growth and lower provisions
data.description:
CSB Bank standalone net profit up 14 per cent to ₹182.72 crore on better net interest incomes and lower provisions in the quarter ended September 30 2026 as against ₹160.33 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The bank’s net interest income (NII) increased 20.4 per cent to ₹509.93 crore in the reporting quarter as against ₹423.56 crore in the year-ago period.

The bank’s advances grew 22.1 per cent to ₹42,383 crore in Q2FY27 as against ₹34712 crore in the same quarter last fiscal. Deposits grew ₹18.25 per cent to ₹46889 crore as against ₹39651 crore in Q2FY26.

Besides robust growth in NII, the bank also cut provisions by 52.7 per cent to ₹30 crore in the recently concluded quarter, as against ₹63.65 crore in the year-ago period. The bank’s net interest margin (NIM) was the same as 3.81 per cent in the year-ago period but increased sequentially from 3.6 per cent in previous quarter.

The bank’s non-profitable assets (NPA) as a share of gross advances reduced 23 basis points to 1.58 per cent from 1.81 per cent in the same quarter last fiscal. NPA as a share of net advances also reduced to 0.33 per cent from 0.52 per cent in Q2FY26.

“We remain focused on sustaining this momentum. In the second half of FY27, we plan to accelerate growth across our key business segments, enabling us to move steadily towards our SBS2030 aspiration of becoming a mid-sized bank,” said Pralay Mondal, MD and CEO, CSB Bank.

data.title: TN CM Vijay’s government to distribute 62 lakh cake pieces to school students on Children’s Day
data.description:
The Tamil Nadu government plans to distribute nearly 62 lakh pieces of cake worth ₹7.54 crore to school students across the State on Children’s Day on November 14. This is the first time that the State government is undertaking Children’s Day as a shared celebration, said a senior government official.

Letters of Acceptance (LoAs) have been issued to four vendors — Britannia Industries, ITC Ltd, Elite Natural Pvt Ltd and Dream Bake Pvt Ltd — for supplying sponge-style slice cakes for the distribution programme, a government order shows.

The cakes will be supplied in different flavours, including fruit, vanilla and chocolate. The selection also includes Sunfeast Dark Fantasy Swiss Roll Chocolates, adding variety to the treats planned for students.

The programme will cover school students across Tamil Nadu, with the government procuring the cakes from the four vendors for distribution on the occasion.

The initiative is meant to make Children’s Day a shared celebration in every government and government-aided school, so that each student, along with the teachers and staff who form the school community, marks the day together, an official said. It is a small gesture from the government that we hope will also strengthen children’s bond with their schools and encourage regular attendance, the official added.

data.title: SBI Capital flags RBI’s ‘inconsistency’ in liquidity management
data.description:
SBI Capital Markets termed RBI’s move to inject liquidity as inconsistent with the monetary policy stance of calibrated tightening, in its Ecowrap report published on October 23, 2026.

The RBI conducted Variable Repo Rate (VRR) auctions to inject ₹2.5 lakh crore in the past week, a move that is seen as opposite to the “calibrated tightening” monetary policy stance stated in the October 2026 monetary policy meeting. In the meeting the RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stressed that the RBI would use appropriate measures to absorb liquidity and signalling tight money regime.

The central bank has also been conducting Variable Reverse Repo Rate (VRRR) auctions to suck-in liquidity. The VRR auction comes against this backdrop.

“The Governor has amplified external conditions and financial stability and less amplified liquidity and transmission as compared to August policy. This clearly shows that RBI is cognizant more of threat to external stability arising from widening geopolitical conflicts even as a rate hike was resorted to with inflation concerns taking centre stage.

We, however, find it a little difficult to understand the reasons behind RBI move to inject liquidity through repo auctions of ₹2.5 lakh crore even as the primary objective is to ensure that the RBI is in a “calibrated tightening” mode and RBI Governor also emphasizing less on liquidity in October policy,” said Soumya Kanti Ghosh, Group Chief Economic Adviser, State Bank of India, who also serves as a member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council.

Ghosh said that RBI was giving contradictory signals on the liquidity management front. “While maintaining daily call rates requirements at 99 per cent with regular OMO/ VRRR, RBI has clearly on the path of calibrated liquidity tightening. However, suddenly RBI had done three repo injection from October 19 onwards amounting to ₹2.5 lakh crore which is incoherent in a calibrated tightening mode. This gives a signal to the market that the central bank is still trying to balance multiple conflicting objectives,” said and further asked if RBI moving from “calibrated tightening” to “mildly calibrated tightening.”

data.title: Bajaj General Insurance names Deepak Reddy CEO designate
data.description:
Bajaj General Insurance’s board on Friday approved the appointment of Deepak Reddy as Chief Executive Officer Designate of the company, effective January 1, 2027.

Reddy will take charge as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Bajaj General Insurance, a subsidiary of Bajaj Finserv Ltd, on April 1, 2027, subject to approval of insurance sector regulator IRDAI.

Tapan Singhel will continue as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer until March 31, 2027, ensuring a seamless transition, Bajaj General Insurance said in a statement.

Sanjiv Bajaj, Chairman and Managing Director, Bajaj Finserv Ltd, said, “Few leaders have the distinction of building an institution from the ground up. Tapan is one of them. From its early years as a joint venture to its evolution into a wholly Bajaj-owned company, he has played a defining role in shaping Bajaj General Insurance into one of India’s most trusted general insurers. Under his leadership, the company has earned a reputation for underwriting discipline, innovation, and an unwavering commitment to customers.”

Singhel’s legacy is not just a successful business, but a strong institution built to endure, Bajaj said. “As India’s insurance sector enters its next phase of growth, the opportunity to protect more lives, livelihoods and businesses is immense. We are delighted to welcome Deepak to lead Bajaj General Insurance into its next chapter. I am confident that Deepak will build on the strong foundation laid by Tapan and his team, unlock new opportunities and take the company to greater heights,” he added.

Deepak Reddy brings over three decades of experience in financial services, having held senior leadership positions at Bajaj Finserv, American Express, Standard Chartered Bank and MIRC Electronics. During his 17-year association with Bajaj Finserv, Reddy played a key role in building and scaling several businesses and, in his most recent role within the Group, led the Rural, Insurance and Gold Loan businesses at Bajaj Finance.

He was also Bajaj Finserv’s first Group Head of Human Resources, bringing together business leadership and organisational development experience. Most recently, he served as Chief Executive Officer of Manappuram Finance, according to the statement.

“When we started this journey, we wanted to build an organisation that would redefine the way insurance is understood, delivered and experienced. We have always believed that our job is not just to sell a policy, but to understand customers’ worries and find ways to address them. That has meant challenging conventional thinking, reimagining distribution, pioneering industry-first initiatives and the conviction to take bold decisions in our customer’s interest,” said Tapan Singhel, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Bajaj General Insurance.

“As Bajaj General Insurance enters its next chapter, I am confident that the new team will continue to push boundaries, find better solutions to customer concerns and stay true to our purpose of ensuring that our citizens can live a life of dignity,” Singhel added.

data.title: BPCL Q2 net profit falls almost 22% to ₹4,863 crore
data.description:
State-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) on Friday reported an almost 22 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) decline in its consolidated net profit at around ₹4,863 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher refinery margins were offset by losses from sale of petrol, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

The PSU oil marketing company (OMC) had incurred a loss of around ₹1,873 crore on a quarter-on-quarter (q-o-q) basis.

BPCL’s consolidated total income during the September quarter this fiscal year stood at roughly ₹1.58 lakh crore compared to ₹1.61 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹1.23 lakh crore in Q2 FY26.

Its consolidated total expenses during Q2 FY27 stood at around ₹1.52 lakh crore against ₹1.66 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹1.15 lakh crore in Q2 FY26.

“The lower profit during April-September 2026 is mainly due to suppressed marketing margin on certain petroleum products which was partially offset by higher refining margin,” BPCL said in its results filing on the BSE.

The company’s marketing margins got impacted as PSU OMCs have been selling petrol, diesel and LPG below market rates to shield the common man from volatile prices due to the West Asia conflict.

As on September 30, 2026, BPCL’s cumulative under recoveries on LPG stood at ₹17,334.40 crore (March 31, 2026: ₹12,318.52 crore).

The company’s refining throughput stood at 10.41 million tonnes (mt) in Q2 FY27, compared to 10.15 mt in Q1 FY27 and 9.82 mt in Q2 FY26.

Domestic sales stood at 13.47 mt in Q2 FY27 against 13.62 mt in Q1 FY27 and 12.67 mt in Q2 FY26. Export volume stood at 0.59 mt in Q2 FY27, compared to 0.51 mt in Q1 FY27 and 0.36 mt in Q2 FY26.

Greenfield refinery

BPCL said that it incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary as a dedicated project company for the proposed greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.

“Establishing the subsidiary will provide a dedicated legal and governance structure to carry out project activities with an initial authorised share capital of up to ₹4,900 crore,” it said.

The incorporation of this entity will support due diligence activities, engagement with lenders and potential partners and development of an optimal financing and partnership structure. The detailed feasibility reports are under finalisation and accordingly the financial investment decision and financial commitments will be considered separately by the competent authorities at the appropriate stage, BPCL added.

data.title: Infosys’ large deal wins strengthen despite uneven regional growth
data.description:
Infosys reported large deal wins with a total contract value (TCV) of $5.2 billion in Q2 FY27, of which 62 per cent was net new business. The wins included a mega deal valued at more than $2 billion. Last quarter, the company’s large deal TCV stood at $3.6 billion.

“We saw very strong large deals, with one mega deal at over $2 billion, which is contributing to our growth into the next financial year also,” CEO Salil Parekh said.

Across industry segments, Life Sciences, Energy, Utilities, Resources & Services, Communication and Financial Services recorded growth, while Manufacturing, Retail, Hi-Tech and other segments declined. Geographically, North America and India reported a decline, while Europe and the rest of the world (RoW) grew.

Biggest challenge

The company’s total headcount rose to 3,32,542 from 3,28,062 in the previous quarter, marking a net addition of around 4,000 employees. Attrition stood at 12 per cent. Infosys hired 8,000 college graduates during the quarter and reiterated its full-year target of approximately 20,000 graduate hires, having completed more than half of that target in the first half of FY27.

Praveen Bhadada, CEO & Managing Director, Neovay Global, said, “Infosys' AI revenue grew 29 per cent in three months and is now more than a tenth of the business. Yet, it expects to grow only 1–2 per cent this year. That gap shows the industry’s biggest challenge right now: turning deal wins and AI demand into revenue growth. Many of today’s large deals are about cutting clients’ costs, using fewer vendors and using AI to do the same work with fewer people. They make revenue more secure, but they start slowly, and clients expect a share of the savings. A big order book no longer turns into revenue as fast as it used to,” he said.

He added that firms are relying on AI and productivity to deliver new work rather than hiring ahead of demand. Margins have held steady, which is a positive. But the test for Infosys over the next few quarters is how quickly these deals start earning revenue, and whether AI work grows fast enough to replace the traditional work it is eating into.”

“Infosys is moving beyond standalone AI initiatives and embedding AI across its services portfolio, including application modernization, engineering, workplace services, and business operations. Continued investments in the Topaz ecosystem, AI platforms, and reusable AI assets demonstrate a clear strategy to make AI a core part of service delivery. By combining proprietary, open-source, and partner technologies, Infosys is creating a more flexible and software-enabled delivery model,” said Biswajit Maity, Sr Principal Analyst at Gartner.

He added that the company’s growing focus on AI agents, automation, and productivity-led transformation suggests it is positioning itself to help clients scale AI adoption and achieve measurable business outcomes while strengthening its role as a long-term transformation partner.

data.title: Mitsubishi Power Completes Retrofit of Darajat Geothermal Power Plant in Indonesia
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Mitsubishi Power, a power solutions brand of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI), has completed the retrofit of Unit 3 at the Darajat Geothermal Power Plant in Indonesia, owned by local geothermal power producer Star Energy Geothermal Darajat II, Limited (SEG), and commenced commercial operation. The renovation has increased the power output from 121 megawatts (MW) prior to the retrofit to 129 MW, making it the largest single-unit geothermal power unit in Indonesia. Geothermal power is a renewable energy source with extremely low CO2 emissions during operation, and this retrofit contributes to Indonesia's decarbonization efforts and increases its renewable energy ratio.

The retrofit project involved a partial upgrade of facilities using steam turbines manufactured by MHI's Nagasaki Shipyard & Machinery Works in Nagasaki. Mitsubishi Power handled the design, manufacturing, and installation support, with local subsidiary PT. Mitsubishi Power Indonesia carrying out the on-site installation work through turnkey project execution. Mitsubishi Power achieved operational performance exceeding guaranteed values, adhered to the contract schedule, and completed the project without any safety incidents. This success is the result of the advanced construction technology cultivated by MHI Group, and Mitsubishi Power Indonesia's strong local project execution capabilities.

A ceremony commemorating the project completion and the re-commissioning of Unit 3 was held on October 14 in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta. Alongside this ceremony, Mitsubishi Power and SEG signed a Technical Study and Cooperation Agreement (TSCA) to begin discussions on using the latest maintenance technologies to increase steam turbine output and enhance the plant's reliability and availability. Under this TSCA, Mitsubishi Power Indonesia will support efforts to maximize the asset value of the power plant by introducing the latest technologies from MHI Group to create and deliver unprecedented value. These initiatives are based on the Innovative Total Optimization (ITO) strategy adopted by MHI Group, which aims to provide ongoing value to customers throughout the equipment lifecycle.

Commenting on the project completion, Shigeo Yakushijin, Executive Vice President, Mitsubishi Power, said: "The retrofit of Unit 3 at the Darajat Geothermal Power Plant increased the power output while achieving operational performance exceeding guaranteed values and was completed in a short timeframe without any safety incident. In particular, by adopting innovative construction methods that leverage our expertise as the original designer and manufacturer, and through turnkey project execution, we significantly shortened the construction period, which we believe demonstrates the new value delivered to customers. With its cutting-edge technology and local service structure, MHI Group will continue to be a trusted partner for customers."

MHI Group will continue to pursue efforts for the widespread adoption of high-performance and reliable technologies, contributing to the stable supply of electricity essential for economic development worldwide, as well as energy decarbonization to protect the global environment. Further, through its ITO initiatives, MHI Group will offer customers new value throughout the product lifecycle, and work to create value that transcends conventional boundaries.

About MHI Group

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) Group is one of the world's leading industrial groups, spanning energy, smart infrastructure, industrial machinery, aerospace and defense. MHI Group combines cutting-edge technology with deep experience to deliver innovative, integrated solutions that help to realize a carbon neutral world, improve the quality of life and ensure a safer world. For more information, please visit www.mhi.com or follow our insights and stories on spectra.mhi.com.

Source: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI)

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO draws record ₹7 lakh crore demand
data.description:
Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) attracted demand exceeding ₹7 lakh crore, with more than 1.38 crore applications, setting a record for investor participation in a public offering globally.

The issue, which closed on Friday, was subscribed 22.2 times, with investors bidding for 655.68 crore shares against 27 crore fresh shares on offer.

Investor response

The public portion of the IPO received bids for 438.26 crore shares against 19.75 crore shares on offer, translating into 22.19 times subscription. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) bid for 345.76 crore shares, subscribing to their portion 70.55 times, while the non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times and the retail portion 2.72 times. The employee and eligible shareholder portions were subscribed 2.93 times and 7.6 times, respectively.

Separately, the anchor book attracted bids exceeding ₹2.5 lakh crore against an allocation of about ₹8,110 crore, or more than 30 times the shares available. Jio Platforms had allotted shares to 212 anchor investors before the public issue opened.

The IPO was subscribed 5.57 times at the end of day 2 on Thursday, with QIBs subscribing 13.29 times their portion, non-institutional investors 5.97 times and retail investors 1.54 times.

At ₹30,213 crore, the issue is India’s largest-ever IPO and is entirely a fresh issue of 27 crore shares, with no offer for sale by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the ₹1,119 price band, it values Jio Platforms at about ₹10.3 lakh crore, or $108.3 billion, making it the most valuable company to go public in India by IPO valuation.

After 2 decades

Jio Platforms is the telecom and digital-services arm of Reliance Industries and serves more than 500 million mobile users. The IPO is the first from the Reliance group in nearly two decades.

The company plans to use up to ₹27,500 crore of the proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its wholly owned subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. The balance will be used for general corporate purposes.

The shares are scheduled to list on October 28.

data.title: VZ, TMUS, T Stocks Face Valuation Pressure From SpaceX Wireless Push But Tower Operators Stand To Gain, Says Citi
data.description:
Key points:
  • Citi sees 29%-32% valuation risk for Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T, with another 4%-16% potential downside from current levels.
  • SpaceX is reportedly seeking access to at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites as it looks to establish a fourth nationwide wireless carrier.
  • Citi views the development as positive for Crown Castle, SBA Communications and American Tower.

Verizon Communications (VZ), T-Mobile US (TMUS) and AT&T (T) stocks came into focus Friday after Citi warned of further valuation pressure on established telecom operators as SpaceX (SPCX) advances plans to enter the U.S. wireless market.

According to a note cited by TheFly, Citi sees 29%-32% valuation risk for the three carriers, with a 4%-16% downside potential from current levels following their pullbacks in 2026.

The firm believes SpaceX is likely to build its own telecommunications company to compete in the U.S. mobile market, rather than become a mobile virtual network operator, an outcome it considers unlikely.

At the time of writing, Verizon (VZ) shares fell more than 1%, while T-Mobile (TMUS) and AT&T (T) declined over 5% each. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘bearish’ for T-Mobile (TMUS) and Verizon (VZ), while AT&T (T) attracted ‘bullish’ sentiment.

SpaceX Eyes 80,000 Cell Sites For Nationwide Wireless Network

SpaceX is seeking access to at least 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. and is in discussions with major infrastructure providers, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The potential leasing agreements, which could be worth billions of dollars, would help SpaceX establish a fourth nationwide wireless carrier to compete with the country's dominant operators, the report said.

SpaceX has also pursued low-band wireless spectrum to complement its Starlink satellites and received Federal Communications Commission approval for 15,000 additional satellites designed to provide mobile service directly to phones.

During SpaceX's earnings call this week, CEO Elon Musk said the company plans to build terrestrial networks to provide broader connectivity wherever SpaceX and Starlink are permitted to operate.

Citi Sees Upside For Tower Operators

While Citi views SpaceX's potential entry as negative for established telecom operators, it considers the reported cell-site plans a net positive for Crown Castle (CCI), SBA Communications (SBAC) and American Tower (AMT).

According to the report, potential cell-site leasing agreements with SpaceX could be worth billions of dollars. Crown Castle, which operates approximately 40,000 U.S. cell towers, is among the companies reportedly in discussions with SpaceX.

Asked about potential leasing talks with satellite-based operators during Wednesday's earnings call, Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant said, “You can assume that we're talking to all parties,” without disclosing specific customer discussions.

Tower Stocks Rally on SpaceX Report

The reported plans have already pressured telecom stocks while lifting shares of tower operators, reflecting investors' differing expectations for the two industries.

At the time of writing, CCI shares surged more than 10% to hit a four-month high, while SBA Communications (SBAC) and American Tower (AMT) gained around 4% and 6%, respectively.

Among tower stocks, retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ for CCI and AMT stock, while sentiment around SBAC stock remained ‘neutral’.

data.title: The Trouble for Lam Research, Applied Materials, and KLA Stock Could Be Just Getting Started — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Chip-equipment stocks haven't performed well lately as investor concerns about the hot pace of artificial-intelligence spending have spooked the market. It could be just the beginning of a steeper drop for these stocks, Citi says.

Shares of Lam Research, Applied Materials, and KLA have all suffered recently.

These companies, which make wafer fabrication equipment that turns raw silicon wafers into microchips, are big beneficiaries of the AI spending boom. Their wafer fabrication equipment is used to manufacture the advanced chips needed to power data centers and AI systems.

However, as sentiment around the AI trade has grown more negative due to concerns around debt and the massive spending needed for data-center buildout, so too has the sentiment around these stocks.

"Investors have increasingly focused on potential downside scenarios," Citi analyst Atif Malik said in a research note late Thursday.

Lam Research stock fell more than 17% last week and has declined nearly 13% this week as of Thursday's close. The company's fiscal-first-quarter earnings on Wednesday narrowly surpassed Wall Street estimates, but ran up against lofty investor expectations for artificial-intelligence-related companies.

Shares of Applied Materials, similarly, sank more than 19% last week and entered Friday's trading session down 8.2% this week. KLA stock has fallen 11% this week after tumbling 15% last week.

The sharp share price declines have brought all three stocks below their 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

Malik says there's more downside potential for the three companies' shares based on analysis of the 2028 wafer fabrication equipment market.

Under the firm's base case scenario for 2028, which includes constraints to the wafer fabrication equipment market, Advanced Materials stock has a $335 price target, KLA has a $130 price target, and Lam Research stock has a $208 price target. Those targets represent about 10% downside for each stock from Thursday's closing price.

The firm has bear case price targets of $259 for Advanced Materials, $105 for KLA, and $164 for Lam Research. Those would imply drops of about 30% from Thursday's closing levels.

This is due to the close correlation between chip-equipment demand and the share price for the companies. Any change in the demand outlook for data centers could drastically change the business outlooks for the companies, according to Malik.

The firm also says that while demand from AI data centers is currently robust, supply shortages could constrain market growth in coming years.

Citi has Buy ratings on all three stocks. Malik has current price targets of $435 on Lam Research, $290 on KLA, and $375 on Applied Materials.

Lam Research stock rose 0.6% to $231.84 on Friday after slumping 12% Thursday. Applied Materials stock gained 1.3% to $380.35 on Friday while KLA advanced 0.4% to $148.33.

With all three stocks below key technical levels and seemingly searching for a bottom, investors may be right to take a pessimistic view.
